title: What type is it?
description:
Write two functions:

```javascript
function describeType(value) { }   // "null", "array", or what typeof says
function copyWith(obj, key, value) { }   // a NEW object: obj's properties plus key set to value; obj unchanged
```

`describeType(null)` is `"null"` and `describeType([1])` is `"array"` (fixing `typeof`'s two oddities); everything else is `typeof value`.
hints: The starter already has the two functions: `value` (or `obj`, `key`, `value`) holds what the test passes in, and `return` hands your answer back (lesson 2.01 covers functions in full). To answer early in one case, write `if (value === null) return "null";`: the `return` runs only when the condition in brackets is true (lesson 1.05 covers `if`).
`Array.isArray(value)` tells arrays apart from other objects, and `value === null` catches null.
`{ ...obj, [key]: value }` copies obj's properties into a new object and then sets the property whose name is in `key`.
